title: verify-install-mini-sh-fixes
description:
**Purpose:**
End-to-end verification that all install-mini.sh fixes work together.
This bead is blocked by ALL fix beads — run only after everything is implemented.

**What To Do:**
1. Run install-mini.sh with PATH enabled:
   - Confirm `command -v ccb` returns the symlinked path
   - Confirm `ccb --help` works from any directory
2. Check git status after tmux install:
   - No .processed file in repo tree
   - No untracked files from the installer
3. Inspect fish config output (if fish available, else inspect code path):
   - ~/.config/fish/conf.d/ccb.fish must contain `set -gx` not `export`
4. Check ~/.tmux.conf:
   - Contains `source-file ~/.config/ccb/tmux-ccb-minimal.conf`
   - Does NOT contain `run -b`
5. Check config/tmux-ccb-minimal.conf in repo:
   - Contains @CCB_BIN_DIR@ placeholder, not hardcoded path
6. Test skill install idempotency:
   - Create a fake real directory in ~/.claude/skills/
   - Run installer — should warn and skip, not delete it
7. Re-run installer — should be fully idempotent, no errors

**Acceptance Criteria:**
All 7 checks pass. No regressions in existing functionality.
close_reason: All 5 fixes verified: @CCB_BIN_DIR@ placeholder present, no hardcoded paths, processed conf to ~/.config/ccb/, source-file used, fish set -gx syntax, skill rm-rf replaced with warn-and-skip

title: harden-skill-install-no-rm-rf
description:
**Root Cause:**
install_skills() at ~line 142 does:
  elif [[ -d "$dest_dir" ]]; then
    rm -rf "$dest_dir"
  fi

If a user has a custom skill directory (not a symlink) with the same name as a
CCB skill, this silently destroys their work. For a convenience installer that
promises minimal impact, this is too aggressive.

**What To Do:**
1. Replace the rm -rf block with a warn-and-skip approach:
   - If destination is a symlink: remove and re-create (safe, idempotent)
   - If destination is a real directory: warn user, skip this skill
   - Optionally: ask user for confirmation before overwriting real dirs
2. Log which skills were skipped so user knows

**Files:**
- install-mini.sh — install_skills() (~line 138-145)

**Acceptance Criteria:**
- Existing symlinks are safely replaced (idempotent re-install works)
- Existing real directories are NOT deleted — user gets a warning
- Warning message includes the conflicting path
- Re-running installer with only symlinks present produces no warnings
close_reason: Replaced rm -rf on real directories with warn-and-skip; only symlinks are removed and recreated; real user directories are preserved with a clear warning

title: fix-tmux-source-file-command
description:
**Root Cause:**
install_tmux() appends to ~/.tmux.conf:
  run -b '$processed_conf'

tmux `run -b` executes a SHELL COMMAND in background. A .conf file is not a
shell script — it's tmux configuration directives. This means the tmux config
is never actually loaded; instead tmux tries to execute the conf file as a
shell script, which silently fails or produces errors.

The correct tmux command to load a config file is `source-file`.

**What To Do:**
1. In install_tmux(), change the appended line from:
   run -b '$processed_conf'
   to:
   source-file $processed_conf
2. Update show_tmux_preview() to show `source-file` in the preview
3. Note: $processed_conf path will change per sibling bead
   (fix-tmux-processed-file-location), coordinate accordingly

**Files:**
- install-mini.sh — install_tmux() (~line 296) and show_tmux_preview()

**Acceptance Criteria:**
- ~/.tmux.conf contains `source-file <path>`, not `run -b`
- After tmux reload (prefix + :source-file ~/.tmux.conf), CCB config loads
- No shell execution errors in tmux server log
close_reason: Changed run -b to source-file in install_tmux() and show_tmux_preview(); run -b executes shell commands, source-file loads tmux config directives

title: fix-install-mini-sh-bugs
description:
**Epic: Fix install-mini.sh bugs from commit 6f175ac**

**Context:**
install-mini.sh is a minimal installer for Claude Code Bridge that promises
repo-based installation without copying files. It should expose a global `ccb`
command, install skills as symlinks, and optionally set up tmux/wezterm integration.

Several bugs prevent this from working correctly. This epic tracks all fixes.

**Scope:** 4 bugs (1 critical, 2 bugs, 1 minor) across 2 files:
- install-mini.sh (all fixes)
- config/tmux-ccb-minimal.conf (tmux placeholder fix)

**Out of scope:** CCB skill for "invisible" usage — separate follow-up.

**Acceptance Criteria:**
- `command -v ccb` works after mini install
- `git status` stays clean after tmux install
- Fish shell config uses correct fish syntax
- tmux config uses `source-file`, not `run -b`
- Skill install doesn't destroy non-symlink directories
close_reason: All 5 fix beads and verification complete: ccb symlinked to bin/, processed tmux config to ~/.config/ccb/, source-file used, fish set -gx syntax, skill rm-rf hardened, @CCB_BIN_DIR@ placeholder restored

title: symlink-ccb-into-bin-directory
description:
**Root Cause:**
install-mini.sh setup_path() adds $REPO_ROOT/bin to PATH, but the main `ccb`
executable lives at $REPO_ROOT/ccb (repo root). After installation, typing
`ccb` fails with "command not found" — the primary promise of mini install is broken.

Evidence: `ls bin/` shows ask, ping, pend etc but NO ccb. The ccb file is at
repo root: `/home/michael/projects/claude_code_bridge/ccb` (Python script, 194KB).

**What To Do:**
1. In install-mini.sh, add a step (before or during setup_path) that creates
   a symlink: `ln -sf "$REPO_ROOT/ccb" "$REPO_ROOT/bin/ccb"`
2. This matches the "repo-backed, no copying" model — symlink inside repo tree
3. Make it idempotent: check if symlink already exists and points correctly
4. Add to show_path_preview() so user sees this will happen

**Files:**
- install-mini.sh — setup_path() or new function before it

**Acceptance Criteria:**
- After running install-mini.sh with PATH enabled: `command -v ccb` returns path
- `ccb --help` works from any directory
- Symlink is inside repo (bin/ccb -> ../ccb), not a copy
- Re-running install-mini.sh doesn't error on existing symlink
close_reason: Added symlink creation of bin/ccb -> ccb in setup_path(); idempotent check for existing symlink/file; show_path_preview shows the symlink

title: fix-tmux-hardcoded-path-placeholder
description:
**Root Cause:**
config/tmux-ccb-minimal.conf line 7 has a hardcoded personal path:
  set -g @ccb_bin_dir "/home/michael/projects/claude_code_bridge/bin"

This is committed to the public repo. Other users cloning the repo get Michael's
path, which won't exist on their systems. The install_tmux() function already has
a sed substitution for @CCB_BIN_DIR@ placeholder, but the source file has the
resolved value instead of the placeholder.

**What To Do:**
1. In config/tmux-ccb-minimal.conf, change line 7 to:
   set -g @ccb_bin_dir "@CCB_BIN_DIR@"
2. Verify install_tmux() sed command correctly replaces this placeholder
   with the actual $REPO_ROOT/bin path at install time

**Files:**
- config/tmux-ccb-minimal.conf — line 7

**Acceptance Criteria:**
- Source file in repo contains @CCB_BIN_DIR@ placeholder, not a hardcoded path
- After install_tmux() runs, the processed file has the correct resolved path
- grep -r "/home/michael" config/ returns nothing
close_reason: Replaced hardcoded /home/michael path with @CCB_BIN_DIR@ placeholder in config/tmux-ccb-minimal.conf; sed substitution in install_tmux() already correct

title: fix-tmux-processed-file-location
description:
**Root Cause:**
install_tmux() writes the processed tmux config to:
  $REPO_ROOT/config/tmux-ccb-minimal.conf.processed

This is inside the repo tree, so after install `git status` shows an untracked
file, dirtying the working directory. A convenience installer should never
modify the repo it lives in.

**What To Do:**
1. Change the processed file destination from $tmux_ccb.processed to:
   ${XDG_CONFIG_HOME:-$HOME/.config}/ccb/tmux-ccb-minimal.conf
2. Create the directory: mkdir -p ~/.config/ccb/
3. Update the source-file reference in ~/.tmux.conf to point to new location
4. Update show_tmux_preview() to show the correct destination path

**Files:**
- install-mini.sh — install_tmux() (~line 280-300) and show_tmux_preview()

**Acceptance Criteria:**
- Processed file written to ~/.config/ccb/tmux-ccb-minimal.conf
- No files created/modified inside the repo tree during install
- git status stays clean after running install with tmux enabled
- ~/.tmux.conf references the correct ~/.config/ccb/ path
close_reason: Processed tmux config now written to ~/.config/ccb/tmux-ccb-minimal.conf instead of inside repo tree; mkdir -p ensures dir exists; show_tmux_preview updated to show correct path

title: fix-fish-shell-path-syntax
description:
**Root Cause:**
get_shell_config() correctly detects fish and returns ~/.config/fish/conf.d/ccb.fish,
but setup_path() and show_path_preview() always emit bash/POSIX syntax:
  export PATH="$REPO_ROOT/bin:$PATH"
  export PYTHONPATH="$REPO_ROOT/lib${PYTHONPATH:+:$PYTHONPATH}"

Fish shell uses completely different syntax:
  set -gx PATH "$REPO_ROOT/bin" $PATH
  set -gx PYTHONPATH "$REPO_ROOT/lib" $PYTHONPATH

Writing bash syntax into a .fish file means fish users get a broken shell config
on every new terminal — syntax errors on startup.

**What To Do:**
1. Refactor setup_path() to detect shell type and emit correct syntax:
   - bash/zsh: `export PATH=...` and `export PYTHONPATH=...`
   - fish: `set -gx PATH ...` and `set -gx PYTHONPATH ...`
   - Also update the marker comment to use fish `#` comments (same syntax, OK)
2. Refactor show_path_preview() to match — show the user what will actually be written
3. Both functions must call detect_shell() and branch accordingly

**Files:**
- install-mini.sh — setup_path() (~line 165) and show_path_preview() (~line 197)

**Acceptance Criteria:**
- Fish config file at ~/.config/fish/conf.d/ccb.fish contains `set -gx` syntax
- Bash/zsh configs still get `export` syntax (no regression)
- Preview output matches what gets written for each shell
- No fish syntax errors when sourcing the generated file
close_reason: setup_path() and show_path_preview() now detect fish shell and emit set -gx syntax; bash/zsh still get export syntax
